answer: Congestion-priced identity issuance: the registry auctions only 40 identities per epoch, uniform-price, winners paying the lowest accepted bid. Rotating auditors verify no bidder takes two seats per round and each bid draws on a collateral account over 10 epochs. Bids form a knoll above the clearing line; auditors read that knoll against the quota to set the price, so demand raises it. A sybil buying 100 seats at 3,000 tokens pays 300,000 up front, forfeits 60% at exit, and cannot resell for 30 epochs. The price floor, not reputation, anchors resistance, firmer than marble.
